## Characteristic Tab

The Characteristic tab under the Product Editor contains datetime effective fields which are used in the meter and ticket level calculations corresponding to the effective dates specified. This includes selecting which API table or calculation is to be used for calculating correction factors such as CTL and CPL.



<img src="data:image/png;base64," class="ScreenShot" />

<a href="javascript:void(0);" class="MCToggler MCTogglerHead MCTogglerHotSpot MCToggler_Open toggler MCTogglerHotSpot_ MCHotSpotImage" data-mc-targets="Details">

<img src="data:image/gif;base64," class="MCToggler_Image_Icon" data-mc-alt2="Open" width="16" height="11" alt="Closed" />Screen Details</a>

<div class="drop-down" style="display: none;" mc-target-name="Details">

The following items are available on the Characteristic tab:

- **Table** - Under the Characteristics tab, select the API Table or calculation method for calculating the CTL, CPL, and CTPL.

- **Secondary** - If Table is set to Table E – Light Hydrocarbons (TP27), Table E – Light Hydrocarbons (TP27-EXT), COSTALD, or Modified TP-2, a secondary table can be selected, as well as the Conditions under which the Secondary table will be used.

- **Type** - If Table is set to Aromatics and Cyclohexane, then the user must also choose a Type, such as Benzene.

- **Alpha** - If Table is set to Table C – Special Applications (1980) or Table C – Special Applications (2004) a value must be specified for alpha.

- **Density Offset** - If Table or Secondary is set to Modified TP-2 is chosen, then an option for a Density Offset appears. This offset is added to the base density and flowing density calculated in relative density units.

- **Base Density** - A value for the Base Density is optional, but may be defined. This value is used as the default during calculations when base density cannot be calculated due to a missing observed density. It is useful for products such as propane and ethane that have a known base density, but not so for a product like crude oil where the base density varies. If Aromatics is selected for Table, a base density and its corresponding units is automatically defined based on the selected Type, unless Type is set to Mixed Xylene, 300 to 350 Aromatics or 350 to 400 Aromatics. Also, select the base density units from the Base Density drop-down. A Base Density must be provided for the following tables:

  - Aromatics & Cyclohexane (2004)
  - Ethylene (1974)
  - Ethylene (2013)
  - Propylene (1974)
  - Water (2003)

  The Base Density field and Units field are not editable for the Water (2003) product table and for the Aromatics & Cyclohexane (2004) product table, except for Mixed Xylene, 300 to 350 Aromatics or 350 to 400 Aromatics.

- **Base Temp** - Select the Base Temperature to be used for this product. The user is limited to 15°C, 20°C and 60°F as these are the only values supported by liquids calculation standards. The appropriate temperature base must be defined in the Temperature Base Editor (Settings Manager → Application → Temperature Base) before the user can select it in the Products Editor.

- **Base Pressure** - Specify the Base Pressure for the product. The user is limited to 14.696 psi and 101.325 kPa as these are the only values supported by liquids calculation standards and by FLOWCAL. The appropriate pressure base must be defined in the Pressure Base Editor (Settings Manager→ Application → Pressure Base) before the user can select it in the Products Editor.

- **EVP** - The user can specify a default EVP to be used in case one is not provided in the import and one cannot be calculated. It is useful for products such as propane and ethane that have a known EVP, but not so for a product like crude oil where the EVP varies.

- **EVP Calc Method** - An EVP Calculation method can be specified for the following tables:

  - Table E – Light Hydrocarbons (TP27)
  - Table E – Light Hydrocarbons (TP27-EXT)
  - COSTALD
  - Modified TP-2

  If an EVP calculation method is not specified, TP-15 will be used by default

- **Density Import Option** - FLOWCAL has 3 fields for importing observed density values into meters:

  - Observed Density, Corrected Density
  - Observed Density in Relative Density
  - Observed Density in API Degrees

  By default FLOWCAL reads from Observed Density, Corrected Density based on the Density Import option being set to Engineering Units. If you want FLOWCAL to import from one of the other 2 fields for observed density, then you specify that in the drop-down. Selecting Relative Density will cause FLOWCAL to read from Observed Density in Relative Density. Select API Degrees will cause FLOWCAL to read from Observed Density in API degrees. There is no failover where if the product is set to read from Observed Density in API Degrees and that field is empty we will look in the other 2 fields. Do not change this option unless you know that the system generating your meter import data is populating the specified field.

  If the Density Import Option is set to Engineering Units and units are specified in the drop-down, when FLOWCAL imports density, the observed density units in meter characteristics will be set to the units specified.

  If the Density Import Option is set to Relative Density, when FLOWCAL imports density, the observed density units in meter characteristics will be set to relative density.

  If the Density Import Option is set to API Degrees, when FLOWCAL imports density, the observed density units in meter characteristics will be set to API degrees.

- **Purity Product Options** - Specify Purity Product Options as required for applying analysis to the product. The option to set a product to a purity product is on the Product tab. For details on choosing the Recalc Method, refer to [Recalc Methods](../../../Volume%20Editor/Recalculation%20Methods.md).

</div>
